newsitem.title: CHINA: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS SAYS RIFT AT BAYERN HEALED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS SAYS RIFT AT BAYERN HEALED.

text.p: Germany's most capped player Lothar Matthaeus said on Thursday his dispute with champions Bayern Munich had been resolved following talks with club boss Franz Beckenbauer.
Matthaeus, who has been widely criticised by Bayern players and Beckenbauer for a series of disparaging remarks, said the disagreement had been settled and he would be staying at Bayern.
"I spoke with the president (Beckenbauer) today and we have solved our problems," Matthaeus said after a tournament here between FIFA and Asian all-stars.
"It was a little problem which became a big one because it's summer in Germany and there is no football," he added. "I'm going to stay next year."
Matthaeus said he would be talking to his Bayern team mates when he returned to Germany. He had irritated many former and current players with critical remarks in recent weeks.
The 36-year-old libero launched his attacks on fellow players and club officials after he was dropped as club captain last month.
He was stripped of the armband for publishing his "Secret Diaries", a behind-the-scenes look at Bayern's season.
But the uproar prompted the increasingly isolated Matthaeus to take a more sober approach and he told the Sport Bild weekly recently that he hoped to continue his career in Munich.
"It would be a shame if everything was to end in such a stupid way," Matthaeus said.

He met Beckenbauer in Hong Kong on Thursday and the two said the meeting had cleared the air. Beckenbauer, who has long supported Matthaeus, had been blaming the former captain for the public row and demanded he keep quiet.
"I didn't expect any other result," Beckenbauer said. "Lothar has a contract that runs until 1998. He will stay with us. I would even recommend he stay for another year or two beyond that."
Matthaeus said he was confident the disputes could be put behind him.
"I have known Franz Beckenbauer for 13 years and we have a friendly relationship," he said.
Asked about discussions with his team mates, he said: "It's important that we speak but not with journalists around."
As far as his future career was concerned Matthaeus said he was contemplating continuing on a "year to year basis" and at the end of his career would probably opt for a job connected with soccer.
